Τί γάρ φησιν ὁ ἱεροκῆρυξ εὐαγγελιστὴς τῆς ἑορτῆς, ἄκουσον· Ἐγένετο ὅτε
ἤγγιζεν ὁ Κύριος εἰς Βηθφαγὴ, καὶ εἰς Βηθανίαν, πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον
Ἐλαιῶν, ἀπέστειλε δύο ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, λέγων· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀπέναντι
κώμην, καὶ ἐν τῷ εἰσελθεῖν ὑμᾶς εὑρήσετε ὄνον καὶ πῶλον δεδεμένην· λύσαντες
ἀγάγετέ μοι. Καὶ ἐποίησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ καθὼς ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ
ὑπέστρωσαν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τὴν πῶλον, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς. Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς
ἤγγισεν εἰς τὴν κατάβασιν τοῦ ὄρους, ὁ ὄχλος ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ἔλαβον βαΐα
τῶν φοινίκων, καὶ ἐξῆλθον εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. Καὶ οἱ προάγοντες, καὶ οἱ
ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ ∆αβὶδ, εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν
ὀνόματι Κυρίου. Αὕτη τῆς παρούσης ἑορτῆς ἡ ∆εσποτικὴ παρουσία· αὕτη τοῦ
Βασιλέως τῶν βασιλευόντων ἡ ἐν Σιὼν πάλαι καὶ νῦν ἐπιδημία· αὕτη τῆς παρούσης
ἡμέρας ἡ λαμπρὰ καὶ πάνδημος τοῦ ποιητοῦ τῶν ἁπάντων ἔλευσις.
∆ιὸ νῦν, ἀδελφοὶ, ὁ ὄχλος ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν, ἐξέλθωμεν εἰς ἀπάντησιν
αὐτοῦ, ὅ τε ὁρατὸς κόσμος καὶ ὁ ἀόρατος, καὶ οἱ προάγοντες χρόνῳ προφῆται, καὶ
διδάσκαλοι, καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ πώλῳ, οἱ Θεῷ πίστει συμφωνοῦντες. Σήμερον
τὰ οὐράνια σὺν τοῖς ἐπιγείοις ὁμοῦ τε καὶ καταχθονίοις ἀνυμνείτω· πᾶν στόμα καὶ
πνεῦμα πρὸς αἶνον Θεοῦ ἀνοιγόμενον. Τὰ χερουβὶμ, βοήσατε, Ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος
Κύριος, ὁ τρισάγιος, σαβαώθ· πλήρης ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ· σεραφὶμ,
ὑμνήσατε· προφῆται, κηρύξατε. Καὶ ὁ μὲν λεγέτω· Εὐφραινέσθωσαν οἱ οὐρανοὶ, καὶ
ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ γῆ· ὁ δὲ, Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιὼν, κήρυττε, θύγατερ Ἱερουσαλήμ·
καὶ ἄλλος τῷ βασιλεῖ Χριστῷ ἀτενίζων βοάτω· Ἴδε ὁ Ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν
ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου· καὶ ἕτερος περὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου κηρυξάτω· Οὗτος ὁ Θεὸς
ἡμῶν· οὐ λογισθήσεται ἕτερος πρὸς αὐ43.436 τόν· καὶ ἄλλος· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος ὁμοῦ
καὶ Θεός. Ἀνατολὴ ὄνομα αὐτῷ· καὶ ∆αβὶδ πρὸς τὸν ἐξ αὐτοῦ κατὰ σάρκα Χριστὸν
ἀτενίζων λέγῃ· Θεὸς Κύριος, καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν· καὶ πάλιν ἄλλος τὸ γόνυ κλίνων
βοάτω Χριστῷ· Πᾶσα ἡ γῆ προσκυνησάτω σοι· καὶ ἕτερος τοῖς λαοῖς ἐπιτρέπῃ, λέγων·
Συστήσασθε ἑορτὴν ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσιν ἕως τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
Οὕτω γὰρ ἐπετελεῖτο καὶ πάλαι ἡ ἐν Σιὼν τοῦ ∆εσπότου μετὰ τοῦ πώλου
ἐπιδημία· πάνδημος συμφωνία, οἱ χοροὶ τῶν πατέρων, οἱ δῆμοι τῶν δικαίων, τὰ
πνεύματα τῶν προφητῶν, οἱ παῖδες τῶν Ἑβραίων, τὰ νήπια τῶν μητέρων, τὰ πλήθη
τῶν ἀγγέλων. Οἱ μὲν πτέρυγας ἐφήπλουν, οἱ δὲ βαΐα κατεῖχον, οἱ δὲ ὄπισθεν
ἤρχοντο, ἄλλοι τοὺς κλάδους ἔκοπτον, ἄλλοι δὲ τοὺς θάλλους ἔπλεκον, οἱ μὲν τὸν
πῶλον ἔλυον, οἱ δὲ χιτῶνας ἐστρώννυον, οἱ μὲν τὰς πύλας ἤνοιγον, οἱ δὲ ὁδοὺς
ἐκάθαιρον, ἄλλοι πῶλον εὐτρέπιζον, ἄλλοι νίκην ἐκήρυττον, ἄλλοι τοὺς κλάδους
ἔσειον, ἄλλοι νηπίοις ἔλεγον, Αἰνεῖτε, παῖδες, Κύριον· οἱ παῖδες ἀπεκρίναντο,
Ὡσαννὰ εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου. Ὢ καινῶν καὶ παραδόξων
πραγμάτων καὶ θαυμάτων τῆς ἑορτῆς!
thought_title: The Gospel account and the universal festal chorus
orientation: Epiphanius quotes the evangelist's account of Christ's entry on the colt, then calls the whole creation, prophets, and children to join the festal praise.
pass_a_gloss: For what does the sacred herald evangelist of the feast say? Listen: It happened when the Lord drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mountain called of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, saying: Go into the village opposite, and as you enter you will find a donkey and a colt (Matthew's account mentions both; the homily focuses on the colt as royal symbol) tied; having untied them, bring them to me. And the disciples did just as Jesus commanded them; and they spread their garments on the colt, and Jesus sat. And it happened as he drew near to the descent of the mountain, the crowd that had come to the feast took palm branches of the date palms, and went out to meet Jesus. And those going before, and those following, were crying out: Hosanna to the son of David, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord (the children's cry in Matthew 21:9; the homily later quotes the shorter form 'Hosanna, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' as the same acclamation). This is the Lord's coming of the present feast; this is the King of those who reign's sojourn in Zion of old and now; this is the bright and all-public arrival of the maker of all things on the present day. Therefore now, brothers, let us, the crowd that has come to the feast, go out to meet him, both the visible world and the invisible, and the prophets and teachers who go before in time, and those who follow the colt, who agree with God by faith. Today let the heavenly things together with the earthly things and likewise the things under the earth sing praise; every mouth and spirit opened for praise of God. Cherubim, cry out: Holy, holy, holy Lord, the thrice-holy, Sabaoth; full is the heaven and the earth of his glory; seraphim, sing hymns; prophets, proclaim. And let one say: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult; and another: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion, proclaim, daughter Jerusalem; and another, gazing at Christ the King, let him cry out: Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world; and another let him proclaim about the Lord himself: This is our God; no other will be reckoned beside him; and another: Behold a man at once and God. East is his name; and David, gazing at the Christ from him according to the flesh, let him say: God the Lord, and he has appeared to us; and again another, bending the knee, let him cry out to Christ: Let all the earth worship you; and another let him urge the peoples, saying: Establish a feast among those adorning up to the horns of the altar. For thus was accomplished also of old the visitation of the Master with the colt in Zion: harmony witnessed by all, the choruses of the fathers, the peoples of the righteous, the spirits of the prophets, the children of the Hebrews (same group as the priests and Hebrews elsewhere), the infants of the mothers, the multitudes of the angels. Some were spreading wings, others were holding palm branches, others were coming from behind, others were cutting branches, others were weaving shoots, some were untying the colt, others were spreading tunics, some were opening the gates, others were cleaning the roads, others were preparing the colt, others were proclaiming victory, others were shaking the branches, others were saying to the infants: Praise, children, the Lord; the children answered: Hosanna, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. O new and paradoxical deeds and wonders of the feast!

choices.why: παρουσία is the fixed glossary term for the Lord's coming; ∆εσποτικὴ marks it as belonging to the Master/Lord
the word means a stay or visit in a place, distinct from παρουσία; 'sojourn' keeps the sense of dwelling among a people
the compound means 'of the whole people'; 'all-public' preserves the πᾶν + δῆμος force without smoothing it away
ἔλευσις is a noun of coming/arrival; distinct from παρουσία and ἐπιδημία in this passage
fixed glossary rendering for the cherubic acclamation
the verb means decking or adorning with foliage, fitting the festal context of Psalm 118:27 LXX

pass_b_english: Listen to what the sacred herald evangelist of the feast says: “When the Lord drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples, saying, ‘Go into the village opposite you, and as you enter you will find a donkey and a colt tied; untie them and bring them to me.’ And the disciples did as Jesus commanded them; they spread their garments on the colt, and Jesus sat on it. And as he drew near to the descent of the mount, the crowd that had come for the feast took palm branches and went out to meet Jesus. Those going before and those following cried out, ‘Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord’” (Matthew 21:1-9). This is the Lord’s coming for the present feast. This is the visitation in Zion, of old and now, of the King of those who reign. This is the bright and public arrival of the Maker of all things on this present day.

Therefore now, brothers, let us, the crowd that has come for the feast, go out to meet him, both the visible world and the invisible, and the prophets and teachers who went before in time, and those who follow the colt, agreeing with God in faith. Today let the heavenly beings sing praise together with the earthly and those under the earth; let every mouth and spirit be opened for the praise of God. Cherubim, cry out: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, the thrice-holy, Lord of hosts; heaven and earth are full of his glory” (Isaiah 6:3). Seraphim, sing hymns; prophets, proclaim. Let one say, “Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice” (Psalm 96:11); another, “Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion; proclaim, daughter Jerusalem” (Zechariah 9:9); and another, gazing intently at Christ the King, let him cry out, “Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world” (John 1:29); and another, let him proclaim about the Lord himself, “This is our God; no other shall be compared to him” (Baruch 3:36); and another, “Behold a man, and his name is the Rising” (Zechariah 6:12); and another, “Behold a man at once and God”. And let David, gazing intently at the Christ who comes from him according to the flesh, say, “God the Lord has appeared to us” (Psalm 117:27a LXX); and again another, bending the knee, let him cry out to Christ, “Let all the earth worship you” (Psalm 66:4); and another, let him urge the peoples, saying, “Bind the festival with wreaths, up to the horns of the altar” (Psalm 118:27).

For so the Master’s visitation in Zion with the colt was celebrated of old as well: a harmony witnessed by all, the choirs of the fathers, the assemblies of the righteous, the spirits of the prophets, the children of the Hebrews, the infants of the mothers, the multitudes of the angels. Some were spreading their wings over him, others held palm branches, others came from behind, some cut branches, others wove shoots, some untied the colt, others spread their garments, some opened the gates, others cleared the roads, some prepared the colt, others proclaimed victory, some shook branches, others said to the infants, “Praise the Lord, children” (Psalm 113:1); the children answered, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.” O what new and astonishing deeds and wonders of the feast!
